spans.text: The night of stalls.
The exuberant crowd flows on.
However, the Commander wanders in distress.
Five minutes ago, at the night market.
Griffin's [Lycan Club] is now recruiting!
The Commander over there! Are you interested?
The Commander turns around and is greeted by a beautifully designed leaflet.
Five-seven is the one handing them out.
Join the Club now and enjoy one-on-one tutoring from me!
Simply vote for me with those cards of yours, and you'll be a member within no time! It's exclusive to tonight!
Thanks, but I'll pass.
Come on... Don't just deny me like that, Commander.
By the way, I'm the Club's vice president, and a known game master.
It's rare for me to teach others how to play the game...
For such a rare opportunity, perhaps you may want to reconsider?
"Vice president"?
Could it be that your president is Springfield?
Huh? How did you know?
Guesswork.
If I recall, Springfield is one of Griffin's best at these social games...
Heh... You're right.
But...
Five-seven suddenly leans into the Commander's ear and mumbles...
Dismissed?!
...Why?
Five-seven shrugs.
To begin with, Miss Springfield does very little for the daily operation of Lycan Club due to her chores at the café.
On top of that, she made the critical mistake of poisoning a Villager as the Witch this afternoon...
Because of that, many members have expressed their dissatisfaction with Springfield being the president.
I'm afraid it won't be long before everyone asks her to resign.
The Commander gazes worryingly at the Witch's stall in front.
I wonder how Springfield is doing now...
Having made such a mistake in her favorite game, even being rejected by her club members...
She must feel really bad.
The Commander ponders, takes a deep breath, and then walks in...
I told you guys earlier we're closed! Werewolves go out and turn left, Villagers to the right!
Pardon me for not escorting you out!
Is that you?
A slender figure suddenly peeks out from behind the table. Her embarrassment reddens her cheeks.
Commander?!
Erm, sorry...
There were a lot of troublemakers earlier. Please don't take it personally!
It's alright...
What was that about those troublemakers you mentioned?
Also, I remember Springfield being the stall master here... Where did she go?
The Commander looks around. WA2000 stands in the tiny stall alone. The silence is oddly deafening.
Blame those babblers. Now she can't even return to her stall...
What exactly happened?
Hey, how are you unaware?
Wasn't that White King Lycan and her leaflets making a big deal about it just now?
I'm afraid the entirety of Griffin now knows Springfield will be forced to resign and is waiting to laugh at her!
...I'm aware of that.
But is it really that severe?
WA2000 nods unnaturally, avoiding the Commander's gaze.
...You're here to play games, right?
Springfield was in a bad mood, so she went on a stroll. I'll tell her to come back...
Y-you need to console her, you hear me?
If it's you, she can probably pull herself together.
If there's anything I can do, I'll do my best.
While looking at the Commander, WA2000 pauses in silence. As she pulls out her terminal, she pouts briefly and dials the call.
Beep—
Sorry, user is unavailable.
Huh?
...? Springfield's signal got blocked?
Let me try.
Beep—
Sorry, user is unavailable.
Co-commander, there's n-no way something happened to Springfield, right?
Did she say anything when she left?
Conversely, did she behave strangely in any way?
Emm... I do remember... she looked quite depressed...
Like... as if she was going to collapse at any moment!
WA2000's voice shivers. She stares blankly at the ground.
Don't worry. She's Springfield, after all. Everything will be fine.
Let's go and find her.
Right, let's split up!
I'll look around the beaches and the Commander at the plaza!
If you find anything, tell me right away!
...Twenty minutes later.
The Commander, with worries still lingering on their mind, walks out of one of the stalls, defeated.
That was the last stall, yet no one saw Springfield...
Where did she go...
No way she really...
Commander? You look worried.
Would you like a cup of coffee?
A familiar voice pulls Commander back into the physical realm.
Suddenly, those all-too-mundane smiling eyes are staring at the Commander.
Springfield?
After blinking repeatedly to make sure it isn't an illusion, the Commander lets out a sigh of relief.
Commander?
Looking at the Commander's obvious unusual behavior, the smile on Springfield's face slowly turns into confusion.
...I've heard about everything, Springfield.
Well, you know... we aren't all-knowing, so everyone makes mistakes.
I know it was probably a big blow to you, but don't let it discourage you.
Don't deny yourself because of a single incident. All of us are...
Springfield's expression turns from being puzzled, to stunned, and finally into an apparent grin. Commander, with their mouth open, realizes something is up.
I got played by WA2000, right?
Huh? What are you talking about?
So are you not going to keep consoling me? I was so sad that I started doubting myself.
Eh...
Against Springfield's teasing, the Commander sighs again.
I knew something was up... Even if the Earth turns upside down, I can't associate Miss Springfield with the word collapse.
However, you still came to console me right away.
I'm very touched by that.
So what are you doing here?
A customer ordered a "Special American Ice Coconut".
But both Miss Gr G36 and Gr G28 forgot the recipe... so they asked me for help.
Springfield hands the still confused Commander a cup of iced coffee.
WA2000 told you everything?
Well... she said, due to the mistakes you made, you're going to lose your title as the club president.
That's not completely false.
I don't think she intentionally lied to you either. She's just concerned about me...
Springfield seems to have thought of something and puts on a bitter smile.
...and the fact that she doesn't want to lose.
What does that mean?
This is my guess, but maybe she's trying to capitalize on your sympathy and get you to vote for us?
If I receive tons of votes, then maybe I won't be discharged from my position... That's probably her line of thought.
The Commander scratches their face.
...What about you?
Hmm?
You just said that these are WA2000's thoughts.
What about you, Miss Springfield? Doesn't it matter to have your reputation questioned? Or being asked to resign by all the other members of the Lycan Club?
Springfield opens her mouth slightly, revealing some signs of vexation.
...Sorry, I didn't mean to bring that up.
No, it's alright.
Seeing the Commander going straight for an apology, Springfield puts on another bitter smile.
Saying that I don't care anymore would be a lie. After all, without the passion and enthusiasm, I would never have taken up the mantle in the first place.
However, this conundrum of mine isn't caused by a single mistake during a single game.
It's the result of my failure to balance the affairs of both sides of my work.
...You're taking charge of too many things.
If someone tries to console me with those kinds of words, it means I have too much work, and they're affecting my efficiency.
As such, wouldn't asking me to reduce my workload be the most logical thing to do?
The Commander is left speechless.
Looking at the Commander, Springfield takes a sip of the coffee, then shows an apologetic expression.
I'm really sorry. Despite you wanting the best for me, I can not reciprocate your wishes.
No, it's okay.
It's a rare sight to see you like this, so it's frankly quite refreshing.
Commander shakes their head.
Although everything you said is correct...
I still feel like those words aren't for me.
It's more like they're there to convince yourself.
Miss Springfield, deep down, you know it wasn't fair, right?
...I really can't argue with you.
I know you quite well, after all.
Springfield stays silent for a moment, then raises her head and downs the half-empty coffee cup in her hand.
You've already heard from WA2000 that I've made a novice's mistake, right?
Yes, though the details are lacking, I got the gist of it.
It's said that you accidentally poisoned a Villager.
Well, this is what actually happened.
A few hours earlier, during the game of "Lycan Sanctuary".
Close your eyes...
Werewolves, open your eyes. Please identify each other.
Mumble... Mumble...
Extremely light whispers emit from somewhere.
Werewolves, choose someone to kill.
You... use comms...
Mumble...
...First... then...
Werewolves, please make up your mind!
Kill... or else...
...Silly...
Mumble... Mumble...
The Witch, please wake up.
Tonight, this person died—
Kalina points at Gr G36.
Would you like to bring her back to life?
Springfield pauses, then shakes her head in silence.
Would you like to poison someone?
Springfield nods, her eyes fixing towards her 11 o'clock—
It's where AA-12, WA2000, and K-PDW sit in a row.
Springfield glances at all three, then slowly raises her finger, pointing it squarely at the one in the middle—WA2000.
Ok!
Please close your eyes.
...That's what actually happened?
Springfield sighs.
The fun in a game like Werewolf lies in all the deceit and mind games.
Only newbies would vote solely on the basis of "I heard a sound coming from that direction."
I do not agree with that statement, but it's quite unavoidable at times.
What does that mean?
It means, there are certain directions that sounds would come from upon the Werewolves making their move.
Even for veterans who should know better than to play like this, their thoughts will still be influenced.
Once these "certain elements" appear, the game's integrity is done for.
Hence, that's why I've always advocated for using private comms.
...I'm confused. If that's what you thought, then why did you poison WA2000?
I guess I did lose my calm...
I simply wanted to eliminate any "saboteur".
The Commander suddenly understands.
... You preemptively poisoned WA2000 just because of noises.
That was a silly solution, wasn't it?
You never considered if she was a Villager or a Werewolf...
Your entire reasoning was the noise.
Ruining their game to prevent them from ruining the game for others.
Even if you don't say it, I know it's quite foolish.
Why didn't you tell everyone out loud?
In that case, I would be directly denouncing those people that made the noise.
Springfield laughs as she answers.
That's how it is...
Now that you have the whole picture...
May I ask for something in return? Commander?
Of course.
When you return to the stall, you must look eager to play games...
Otherwise, WA2000 would think that her plan has failed and be quite upset. She'll likely throw a tantrum at me.
You mean...  concerning the votes?
She must have thought that by being pitiable, you would feel bad and then vote for us.
...That sounds like her.
WA2000 is a naive girl.
She's looking out for me in her own way. Please don't put the blame on her.
Right...
The Commander pauses.
...If, and I say if.
If she gets what she wants, that is you receiving the most votes at the ballot.
Would the predicaments you're facing really improve?
Perhaps...
If the Villager wins, that means I win as well.
With a happy ending like that, maybe people would stop caring about my little mishap.
Who knows?
Truth be told, I really don't want to leave either.
This incident reminded me that I've been slacking off for too long.
If given the chance, I want to be able to make up for my mistakes.
...I understand.
Commander, what took you so long?!
Shouting from WA2000 interrupts the Commander's thoughts.
The Commander looks up, only to realize that they've already made it back to the Witch's stall.
Ho-how's it going? Is Springfield feeling better?
Now that I'm fully aware of Springfield's predicament...
Rest assured, I will be helping her!
Springfield turns her head at the Commander and smiles.
As always, her smile possesses the magical power to soothe anyone.
Influenced by her mood, the Commander walks into the Witch's stall...
Stall master Springfield now announces the opening of the Witch's Hut!
Beep.
Although our original ploy failed, the plan succeeded overall...
It would have been a lot easier to just throw a small temper tantrum.
You were the one complicating things and constantly changing your mind.
What if the Commander didn't take the bait?
Well... that's because I know the Commander really well.
If we went with an act, then I'm sure the commander would have figured it out right away.
Instead, being honest and telling the truth would actually make the Commander consider our request seriously.
Y-you mean I don't know the Commander well enough?!
It's time to duel! Springfield!
Hehe... sorry! Please accept my apology!
Beep. End of communication.
